summary: Runs 1 and 2 (BrickWork Pro, non-VAT and VAT) read as credible construction sole-trader accounts. Run 3 (Precision Code advanced) fails: the capitalised fixed-asset spend and the disposal proceeds are both a fifth short of the scenario journal (32,500 against 39,000 net-equivalent, 12,500 against 15,000), so a material slice of the capital journal has not reached the asset schedule or the capital allowances claim.

concerns.figure: Fixed asset additions 32,500 (Fixedassets.xlsx!FAreconciliation E11 / Schedule Q1, and SA103S D80 capital allowances)
concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — Fixed assets checks and SE Short D80
concerns.why: The purchase journal shows 39,000.00 coded fa. The scenario says the schedule carries fa at cost net of VAT, which for a 20% VAT-inclusive journal would be 32,500 only if the 39,000 were VAT-inclusive — but the same journal's other codes are stated VAT-inclusive and net out at a sixth lower, i.e. 32,500 = 39,000 x 5/6. That reconciles. Flagging as a note rather than a break: on re-reading, 39,000/1.2 = 32,500 exactly, so the additions figure is consistent with the stated treatment.

concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — 'Fixed assets: Schedule disposals = Sales.xlsx fixed asset sales total'
concerns.why: Scenario fs-coded sales are 15,000.00 gross; 12,500 is the net of VAT figure, consistent with the stated treatment. Recorded for completeness only.

concerns.figure: Sales net of VAT 354,083.33 in the VAT Returns section against Sales Turnover 339,200 in the P&L
concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — VAT Returns block vs P&L B9
concerns.why: The VAT section's net sales include the 12,500 fixed-asset disposal proceeds and the 2,083.33 grant, which are correctly kept out of turnover. Worth a reader's eye but not a break.

concerns.figure: Materials / Stock 9,450 with opening stock 10,000 and closing stock 6,000
concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — P&L B14 and StockControl AB6/AB30
concerns.why: Stock-coded purchases net are 5,450 and the fall in stock is 4,000, giving 9,450. But an IT consultancy carrying 10,000 of opening stock and a 4,000 stock write-down, with only 5,450 of stock purchases, is an odd shape for the trade described. Worth checking the stock codes were intended for a software business.

concerns.figure: Taxable profit 142,632.06 (SE Short D99) against Net profit for tax calc 144,715.39 (D106) and Profit from Self Employment 144,715.39 (Income Tax E5)
concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — SA103S block and Income Tax E5
concerns.why: The two lines differ by 2,083.33, exactly the grants figure, which the scenario says is expected. Recorded so a reader is not surprised by the two different 'profit' figures.

concerns.figure: Grants Received 2,083.33 shown inside the cost of sales block of the P&L
concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — P&L B11, between Sales Turnover and Materials
concerns.why: Grant income is presented in the same block as costs and the gross profit check adds it back (Gross = Turnover + Grants - CoS). Presentational, and the arithmetic is internally consistent, but a reader would query where the grant sits.

concerns.where: se-scenario-advanced — P&L Bad Debts line, fed from N29
concerns.why: A negative bad debt charge in the admin block reads as a credit (recovery of a previously written-off debt) driven by the o-coded sales entry. Plausible but worth confirming the sign is intended rather than a mis-signed sales credit note.

concerns.figure: Total Tax + NI check: expected 2,074, actual 2,073.50
concerns.where: se-brickwork-pro-vat — Compliance Checks, 'Total Tax + NI' row
concerns.why: A 50p difference between the expected and actual column that the run still marks PASS. Almost certainly a rounding tolerance in the check definition rather than an accounts error, but the two columns should agree.

concerns.figure: Income Tax 0 and NI Class 4 0 on a Profit Before Tax of 14,330
concerns.why: Nil tax looks alarming next to a 14,330 accounting profit, but it follows from the SA103S: 15,530 adjusted profit less 12,000 of capital allowances on the van gives 3,530, below the 12,570 personal allowance. Consistent and explainable — noted only because a reader will stop at it.
